newsitem.title: CANADA: Calgene to launch gene-altered canola oil.
newsitem.headline: Calgene to launch gene-altered canola oil.

text.p: Calgene Inc plans to introduce genetically-altered canola oil products in the food and industrial markets in 1997, a company spokeswoman said.

"The first product that we have is the laurical canola which will be sold into the food ingredients markets in 1997. It's not produced in Canada right now but that will be one of the primary target areas where we will be growing," Calgene spokeswoman Carolyn Hayworth said in a telephone interview.
Calgene is a California-based company which specializes in genetic engineering. Canola has the lowest level of saturated fat of any oilseed.
Calgene and Canada's largest grain handler, Saskatchewan Wheat Pool, announced earlier Tuesday they entered an agreement to develop and grow genetically-altered canola.
Laurical fatty acids occur naturally in palm, kernel and coconut oil but not in canola oil, Hayworth said.

Laurical fatty acids are used in canola-oil based margarine, cooking oil and other foods, resulting in a better taste and melting action. It also helps lift dirt from fabric in canola oil-based soaps.
SWP will produce 500,000 acres of the genetically altered canola for Calgene.
Hayworth would not disclose the dollar value of the agreement.
The canola will then be crushed in Canada at CanAmera Foods, which is owned in part by SWP, SWP research and development manager Bob Morgan said.
The canola oil will then be sold back to Calgene which has contracts with end users, Morgan said.
